Radio Netherlands: Belgians to Decriminalise Cannabis
From Radio Netherlands Press Review
January 19, 2001

Three of the morning dailies carry items about the Netherlands' neighbour, Belgium, and the fact that it will soon permit the use of cannabis. The left-of-centre DE VOLKSKRANT attaches enough importance to the story to put it on its frontpage.

As in the Netherlands, possession of cannabis for personal use is to be decriminalised. But, the paper points out that the Belgians, as opposed to the Dutch, " are not going to specify a maximum allowable quantity ", because " it wants to avoid giving the impression that small amounts are harmless ". A spokesman for the Belgian government comments that " for some people, five grams (which is the maximum allowed in the Netherlands) is too much ".
(MarijuanaNews note: This is an odd error for RNW. The Dutch personal use limit is 30 grams. The limit per purchase is 5 grams, which would obviously be irrelevant in this context. Coffeeshops can have an inventory of 500 grams. It would appear that in having no limit the Belgians may be more liberal than the Dutch.)
See
An Official Statement On The Netherlands’ Drug Policy; Published In The Most Improbable Place

Belgium will continue to maintain its ban on over-the-counter sales of cannabis. But cultivation of the substance for personal use will be OK. Belgium is also launching a 12-million euro drugs prevention campaign. While this would seem to be an inconsistent policy, the Belgian Health Ministry sees it differently. A spokesman says " a drug-free society doesn't exist. We want to make people aware of the risks. Prevention is better than treatment. Treatment is better than punishment ".
(MarijuanaNews note: The Belgian capital, Brussels, is also the headquarters for the European Union, so this will have a significant impact and take a lot of pressure off the Dutch. The border between Holland and Belgium is open.

There are still checks at the Belgian/French border. It will be interesting to see how the French react to this.)
